$comment: What a DEPLOYED cezar means, as probes a machine can run. The `deploy` step of the
spec-to-deploy workflow is green only when EVERY target below exits 0 — see
cezar is TWO services and shipping one alone used to end that step green.
Each probe runs with bash -lc in the step's cwd, bounded at 60s.
DELIVERY IS NOT ACTIVATION: the service probe deliberately checks that the running
process answers, not merely that a new dist tree was copied into place — a half-live
deploy (new CLI tree, old resident server) is exactly what reads like a whole one.

targets.name: cezar service (backend) — deployed tree matches HEAD and the running process answers
targets.probe: set -e; test -f /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/dist/index.js; test "$(cat /opt/cezar/.deployed-commit 2>/dev/null)" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"; curl -fsS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:4321/api/v1/health > /dev/null

targets.name: cezar UI (web) — the built bundle is the one being served
targets.probe: set -e; test -f /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/web/dist/index.html; curl -fsS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:4321/ | grep -qF "$(grep -o 'assets/index-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.js' /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/web/dist/index.html | head -1)"
